newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Star Entertainment baffled by price rise.
newsitem.headline: Star Entertainment baffled by price rise.

text.p: Star Entertainment (International Holding) Ltd said on Monday it knew of no reasons for the recent rally in its share price and turnover.
The company said its controlling shareholder, Dorest Co Ltd, had confirmed to the directors that it had had no dealings in the shares since the close of a general offer on August 5, 1996.
Star Entertainment has risen HK$0.66 or 122.22 percent to HK$1.20 since it proposed a HK$268.80 million eight-for-one rights issue on September 7.
Trading in the shares was suspended on Friday. They fell HK$0.05 to HK$1.15 by midday Monday.
Star Entertainment also said an associate of Dorest, Win's Entertainment Co Ltd, expected to produce eight films in 1997.
Star Entertainment said Win's, which owns a television production studio in Shenzhen just over the border in China, had hired a television programming team.

The company also said it expected to obtain the distribution rights for over 200 hours of television programmmes produced by Win's in 1997 and to buy a further 200 hours from independent third parties.

Earlier this month, Star Entertainment reached an agreement with Win's giving it the right to distribute films and television dramas produced by Win's and its subsidiaries in the past and for three years in the future.
Star Entertainment said it would seek to buy titles from producers in Hong Kong, China and Taiwan. It may also consider purchasing non-Chinese language films.
The company said it intended to commit substantial amounts of capital to film distribution and television programming.
It said margins in the Hong Kong video distribution market were tight and competition was fierce.

"It is difficult for the the directors to make a reliable estimate of the company's revenue due to the nature of the entertainment business which is dependent on the changing tastes of the public," company chairman Tiffany Chen said.
